event_overview.title: About Syria Conflict
event_overview.subject: Syria Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Syria conflict began with anti-government protests in March 2011 and escalated into armed conflict involving Syrian state forces, opposition armed groups, extremist organizations and foreign actors. It has produced a major humanitarian and displacement crisis, while international efforts have combined diplomacy, humanitarian relief and mechanisms intended to support accountability for serious international crimes.

facts.label: Origin and location
facts.value: The conflict began in Syria in March 2011, after protests that started in Dar'a spread following the violent suppression of demonstrations.

facts.label: Political framework
facts.value: UN Security Council resolution 2254, adopted in 2015, remains the UN-backed framework cited for pursuing a Syrian-led, negotiated political settlement rather than a military solution.

facts.label: International accountability mechanism
facts.value: The UN General Assembly established the International, Impartial and Independent Mechanism (IIIM) on December 21, 2016, to assist investigations and prosecutions of those responsible for the most serious crimes under international law committed in Syria since March 2011.

facts.label: Legal scope
facts.value: The IIIM is not itself a court: it collects, consolidates, preserves and analyzes material and prepares case files for use by competent jurisdictions, subject to human-rights and fair-trial standards.

facts.label: Humanitarian and regional impact
facts.value: The conflict has displaced Syrians both within the country and across the region; UNHCR identifies Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon and Türkiye among the countries affected by the Syria emergency.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: The war has driven large-scale displacement, damaged civilian infrastructure and left millions of people in need of assistance; UNHCR describes it as an ongoing full-scale war and humanitarian emergency.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is the 2026 armed conflict involving the United States, Iran and Israel, centered on attacks, counterattacks and threats affecting Iran, neighboring states and maritime traffic in and around the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. U.S. officials said combat operations began on February 28, 2026, citing self-defense, protection of regional forces and allies, and freedom of maritime commerce; the United Nations has called for de-escalation, protection of civilians and compliance with international law.

facts.label: Start and parties
facts.value: The conflict’s current phase began on February 28, 2026. The United States notified the UN that it had commenced combat operations against Iran in cooperation with Israel; the UN Secretary-General also described subsequent Iranian attacks affecting Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

facts.label: Geographic focus
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz—between Iran and Oman, linking the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea—is a central theater because its security directly affects regional shipping and energy exports.

facts.label: Maritime and energy stakes
facts.value: Disruption to shipping through Hormuz has been a major international consequence: EIA reported that military action and the resulting de facto closure sharply reduced oil flows and contributed to large price increases in early 2026.

facts.value: Voters who participated in South Carolina’s June Democratic primary were ineligible for this Republican special primary; voters who participated in the June Republican primary or did not vote in either June primary were eligible.

event_overview.title: About Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.subject: Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.summary: The Russia-Ukraine War is an ongoing armed conflict between Ukraine and the Russian Federation, rooted in fighting that began in eastern Ukraine in 2014 and greatly escalated with Russia’s full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022. It has involved conventional ground operations as well as long-range missile and drone attacks, and has produced a major humanitarian and displacement crisis.

facts.label: Origins and escalation
facts.value: Conflict-related humanitarian operations in eastern Ukraine expanded in 2014; Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022 transformed the conflict into a nationwide emergency.

facts.label: Main parties and geography
facts.value: The war principally involves Ukraine and the Russian Federation, with military operations taking place in Ukraine and attacks increasingly affecting areas beyond the immediate front line.

facts.label: International legal position
facts.value: On March 2, 2022, the UN General Assembly deplored Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, demanded that Russia end its use of force and withdraw its forces, and reaffirmed Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders.

facts.label: International Court of Justice proceedin
facts.value: In provisional measures issued on March 16, 2022 in Ukraine v. Russian Federation, the International Court of Justice ordered Russia to suspend military operations begun on February 24, 2022, while stating that the order did not decide the case’s merits.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: The war has driven large-scale displacement, damaged civilian infrastructure and left millions of people in need of assistance; UNHCR describes it as an ongoing full-scale war and humanitarian emergency.

items.title: Rescue Teams Save Woman After 36 Hours Trapped in Colombia Earthquake Rubble
items.text: A 32-year-old woman was rescued alive after being trapped for 36 hours under the rubble of a collapsed building in Pereira, Colombia, following a 7.4-magnitude earthquake. Rescuers located her 10 hours before successfully reaching her, as they continue to search for more survivors amid the devastation.

items.title: David Crowley Wins Wisconsin Democratic Primary, Set to Face Tom Tiffany
items.text: David Crowley, the Milwaukee County executive, has won the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor, defeating progressive candidate Francesca Hong. Crowley, who was backed by Governor Tony Evers, will face Republican Representative Tom Tiffany in the upcoming November election. This victory marks a notable shift in the Democratic primary landscape, as Crowley represents a more moderate stance compared to Hong's democratic socialist platform.

items.text: A Syrian court has sentenced former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia for war crimes and crimes against humanity related to the civil war. The court's decision comes after both men were found responsible for their actions in the conflict, which has resulted in approximately 500,000 deaths.
